answer: Use an Amber Crossing Permit: a new agent earns one permit by locking 70 POA for 45 days and completing 6 verified tasks in 18 days, each reviewed by two peers staking 20 POA. A tundra registry publishes every crossing in public, so duplicate work is caught by a single lookup, and a fable-style case file records how each task was actually done. A juniper stamp on each file links it to one verified device. Faking 100 agents locks 7,000 POA, needs 600 tasks, and risks 4,000 POA in stakes. Like printing 100 boarding passes for one seat, a Sybil pays for every pass and is stopped at the gate.
